[[File:Prumnopitys andina in Christchurch Botanic Gardens 04.jpg|thumb|right|''Prumnopitys andina'' foliage]]
'''''Prumnopitys andina''''', the '''lleuque''' or '''Chilean plum yew''',<ref name=forest>[http://forums.forestresearch.gov.uk/newsrele.nsf/web-allbysubject/8EF49E28F1FD5264802571CE0044B3F8 British Forestry Research] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110816155108/http://forums.forestresearch.gov.uk/newsrele.nsf/web-allbysubject/8EF49E28F1FD5264802571CE0044B3F8 |date=2011-08-16 }} on ''P. andina''</ref> is an [[evergreen]] [[Pinophyta|coniferous]] [[tree]] native to south-central [[Chile]] and a few areas in adjacent parts of westernmost [[Argentina]] from 36 to 40° South latitude. It lives on moderately wet soils, preferably on Andean slopes from {{convert|500|–|1100|m|ft|sp=us}}.

==Description==
It grows up to {{convert|30|m|ft|abbr=on}} high, with a trunk up to {{convert|2|m|ft|abbr=on}} in diameter. The [[leaf|leaves]] are linear to sickle-shaped, 15–30 mm long and 2 mm broad. The [[conifer cone|seed cones]] are highly modified, reducing to a central stem 2–4 cm long bearing 1–4 scales, each scale maturing berry-like, oval, 10–15 mm long and 10 mm broad, green maturing dark purple, with a soft edible pulp covering the single [[seed]]. The seeds are dispersed by [[bird]]s, which eat the 'berries' and pass the seeds in their droppings. Seeds are very difficult to germinate. It has a straight and cylindrical trunk, with gray and shiny bark.

==Taxonomy==
This species was formerly placed in the related genus ''[[Podocarpus]]'' as ''Podocarpus andinus''. It was also briefly moved to ''Prumnopitys spicata'' in 1999,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Molloy |first1=B. P. J. |last2=Munoz-Schick |first2=M. |title=The correct name for the Chilean conifer Lleuque (Podocarpaceae) |journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany |date=1999 |volume=37 |issue=2 |pages=189–193 |doi=10.1080/0028825X.1999.9512626 |bibcode=1999NZJB...37..189M }}</ref> however this move was soon after shown to be in error and it was reverted.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mill |first1=Robert R. |last2=Quinn |first2=Christopher J. |title=''Prumnopitys andina'' reinstated as the correct name for "lleuque", the Chilean conifer recently renamed ''P. Spicata'' (Podocarpaceae) |journal=Taxon |date=2001 |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=1143–1154 |doi=10.2307/1224733 |jstor=1224733 |bibcode=2001Taxon..50.1143M }}</ref>

==Uses==
The fruit (an [[aril]]) are {{convert|1.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, blue-purple in color, are eaten by [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native American]] people in Chile, and a marmalade is produced with them. The tree is also occasionally grown as an ornamental tree and a [[hedge (gardening)|hedge]] in oceanic climate areas in northwest [[Europe]] and the [[Pacific Northwest]] of [[North America]]. In these areas, it is also sometimes known as "plum-yew" or "plum-fruited yew", though these names are more commonly applied to plants in the genus ''[[Cephalotaxus]]''.

The wood is a yellowish color and has a good quality. It is used in furniture and construction.

==Conservation==
Evidence suggests that very little regeneration is occurring to replace current ageing trees in populations. In 2007, the [[Forestry Commission]] planted large numbers of young trees at [[Bedgebury Pinetum]] in the UK as part of a project aiming to conserve the [[genetic resources]] of endangered conifers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bedgeburypinetum.org.uk/TheTrees/ |title=The Trees |publisher=Friends of Bedgebury National Pinetum |access-date=15 December 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091105204931/http://www.bedgeburypinetum.org.uk/TheTrees/ |archive-date=5 November 2009 }}</ref>
